result.summary: This PR adds a new kernel C API, btck_chainstate_manager_validate_block, that lets a caller validate a block using a caller-provided set of spent coins instead of the node's own UTXO set. It introduces a CoinsViewBlock class that fetches coins via a callback, wires this through ChainstateManager::ValidateBlock (calling CheckBlock, ContextualCheckBlock, and ConnectBlock with fJustCheck=true), and adds supporting C API endpoints (outpoint creation/equality, coin creation, coinbase check). Extensive kernel wrapper and test additions accompany the change, exercising the new path against regtest blocks.
result.problem: External software that wants to validate a Bitcoin block (miners building on top of Stratum-like flows, alternative light clients, independent verifiers) currently has no way to do so through the kernel library without maintaining a full UTXO set, forcing them to run a complete node just to check one block's validity.

open_concerns: ajtowns and purpleKarrot argue the callback-based coin lookup risks nondeterminism/inconsistency and unnecessary copying, and propose a btck_CoinsDb container type instead; not implemented
nervana21 asks whether ConnectBlock's assumevalid/script-check-skip logic should be forced off when called via this new entry point; unanswered
optout21 suggests a direct (non-kernel) test for ChainstateManager::ValidateBlock and a test exercising a full caller-side UTXO set rather than just the block's own undo data; unaddressed
BIP30 cannot be fully checked through this path (documented limitation, but noted as an edge case in review)
resolved_concerns: Switched from two flattened arrays (outpoints+coins) to a callback-based fetch, addressing purpleKarrot/ismaelsadeeq's concern about double-copying the UTXO set
Height overflow validation added to btck_coin_create per ismaelsadeeq's comment
Redundant block-txid intra-block-spend check removed per ismaelsadeeq's comment
Various documentation nits (confirmation height wording, log message clarity) addressed in the 2026-08-06 push

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Adds a new public ChainstateManager::ValidateBlock method in validation.h/.cpp that invokes CheckBlock, ContextualCheckBlock, and ConnectBlock(fJustCheck=true) against caller-supplied coins, a new validation-facing entry point requiring validation expertise to review correctly.
categories.rationale: Does not alter existing consensus rules or chainstate behavior (existing ConnectBlock/CheckBlock logic is reused unchanged), so it is not a validation-critical change, but nervana21's open question about assumevalid/script-check interaction ('should there instead be some logic that forces a script_check_reason when ValidateBlock calls ConnectBlock') shows a real correctness question specific to validation semantics that a validation reviewer, not just a kernel reviewer, should weigh in on.

uncertainties: Whether the eventual API will look like the current callback design or ajtowns's proposed btck_CoinsDb container, which affects how much of the current diff survives review
Whether nervana21's assumevalid/script-check concern reflects an actual correctness gap or is already handled elsewhere in ConnectBlock
Exact weight to give the still-open design debate when scoring reviewability vs treating it as ordinary iterative review
result.card: Adds a kernel C API (btck_chainstate_manager_validate_block) letting external callers validate a block against a caller-supplied set of spent coins instead of the node's full UTXO set, by wiring a new ChainstateManager::ValidateBlock into CheckBlock/ContextualCheckBlock/ConnectBlock. This serves external kernel consumers (e.g. miners, light validators, the rust-bitcoinkernel project) who want to check block validity without running a full node's UTXO set, a stated kernel-library use case; alexanderwiederin built and validated an external Rust test harness against the current design. Review has been substantial and mostly positive (concept/approach ACKs from yuvicc, nervana21, w0xlt, a thorough code-review ACK from ismaelsadeeq), but ajtowns still argues the callback-based coin lookup should be replaced with a dedicated in-memory coins-container type to avoid copies and nondeterminism, and that thread trailed off unresolved. The PR needs a rebase (mergeable_state dirty, Needs rebase label) and nervana21 raised an unanswered question about how ConnectBlock's assumevalid script-check skip interacts with this new entry point. No dependency PRs block it, though it overlaps conceptually with the closed #32317 and open #36066 on separating UTXO access from validation.
